title: Machines at the Desk
text:
Automation is reshaping the labour market faster than most governments anticipated. Routine clerical and manufacturing tasks are increasingly performed by software and robots, which has raised concern about widespread redundancy. Yet historical evidence suggests that technological change has also created entirely new occupations that were impossible to foresee. The critical question is whether workers can acquire new skills quickly enough to take advantage of these emerging roles.

Economists remain divided on how the transition will unfold. Optimists point to productivity gains that could raise living standards, while pessimists warn that the benefits may accrue mainly to those who own capital. Consequently, many analysts advocate lifelong learning programmes and social safety nets that cushion displaced workers. Whether these measures will be implemented in time is far from certain.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, what concern has been raised about routine clerical and manufacturing tasks?
options: They are becoming more expensive to perform
They are increasingly performed by software and robots
They are being moved to other countries

questions.text: What do optimists point to, according to the second paragraph?
options: Productivity gains that could raise living standards

questions.text: What does the author imply about the historical effect of technological change?
options: It has never created new jobs
It has tended to create occupations that could not have been predicted
It always leads to permanent unemployment

questions.text: What can be inferred about the pessimists' view of the benefits of automation?
options: They believe the benefits will be shared equally
They suspect the benefits will mainly go to capital owners
They think governments will ban robots
They expect no economic benefits at all

paragraph_translations: A automação está remodelando o mercado de trabalho mais rapidamente do que a maioria dos governos previa. Tarefas administrativas e de produção rotineiras são cada vez mais executadas por softwares e robôs, o que gerou preocupação com a dispensa generalizada de funcionários. No entanto, evidências históricas sugerem que a mudança tecnológica também criou ocupações inteiramente novas, impossíveis de prever. A questão crucial é se os trabalhadores conseguirão adquirir novas habilidades com rapidez suficiente para aproveitar esses papéis emergentes.

Os economistas continuam divididos sobre como a transição se desenrolará. Os otimistas apontam para ganhos de produtividade que poderiam elevar o padrão de vida, enquanto os pessimistas alertam que os benefícios podem se acumular principalmente para os donos de capital. Consequentemente, muitos analistas defendem programas de aprendizagem contínua e redes de proteção social que amparem os trabalhadores deslocados. Se essas medidas serão implementadas a tempo é algo longe de ser certo.
